solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Place name to mark round mount

indicators.note: round says the first pair of pieces is wrapped about the next one

parts.note: M stands for the mark, the old German currency
a mount is a horse or pony to ride

explanation.surface: An instruction to label something by drawing a circle round a mountain on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a hill, which fits the map picture, but it is a riding animal. TOM goes 'round' PONY.
explanation.definitionFit: A toponym is the technical term for a word naming a location, such as a town or river.

clue.text: Splash article around some very elevated rival mastheads here?

definitions.text: some very elevated rival mastheads here?

indicators.note: around means scattered about, so the letters of both words are mixed

explanation.surface: A newspaper splash about a rivalry between mastheads, a paper's title banners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splash' and 'masthead' suggest newspapers; the mastheads are tops of masts, high on rival ships.
explanation.definitionFit: In a tall ships race, big sailing vessels compete, their mast tops very high in the air.

clue.text: Around north-east, rebuilding M1 put lots of cones here

indicators.note: Around says the rebuilt letters go round the compass point
rebuilding says these letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: M1 gives M and I, the 1 read as the Roman numeral
NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: Roadworks on the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway, in the north-east have put out many traffic cones.
explanation.walkthrough: The cones are fir cones, not traffic cones.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinetum is a plantation of conifers, trees that bear many cones.

clue.text: Somebody unimportant — or the chief?

definitions.meaning: a nobody, a person of no consequence
read as No. 1, number one is the boss or chief

explanation.surface: Is this person a nobody or the boss?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as 'No. 1'.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-one is a nonentity; split as number one it is the top person.

clue.text: Crew ate gutted eastern fish

parts.note: a crew is men
had means ate, as in had lunch

indicators.note: gutted removes the insides of the word eastern, leaving only its ends

explanation.surface: The ship's crew ate a fish from the east once it had been cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' fits fish but works on the word 'eastern'.
explanation.definitionFit: The menhaden is an Atlantic fish of the herring family, used for oil and bait.

clue.text: Restriction on movement of dog — nowhere near common

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
if things are few they are far from common

explanation.surface: A rule about where a dog may roam, banning it from the village common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' looks like the noun for public grassland; here it is the adjective, and 'nowhere near common' means scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: A curfew is an order keeping people indoors during set hours, limiting their freedom to go out.

clue.text: Worries over small pet

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the worries above the next piece

parts.note: cares are worries

explanation.surface: An owner frets about a tiny pet animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like a noun after 'small'; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet an animal or person is to stroke them fondly, which is to caress.

clue.text: Reprove about stiffly formal, logical operation

parts.note: re means about, concerning
prim means stiffly proper
AND is a logical operation in Boolean logic

explanation.surface: A stiff, rational person gives a rebuke.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprimand someone is to rebuke them formally, the same as reproving.

clue.text: Very serious sign of what is to come

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means intensely serious

definitions.text: sign of what is to come
definitions.meaning: a token or pledge of more to follow

explanation.surface: Something grave foreshadows trouble ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and grave; as a noun it is a pledge, a foretaste of the future.

clue.text: Get one who's in debt taking in new man of property

parts.note: to land something is to get or secure it

indicators.note: taking in says one piece swallows the next one

parts.note: an ower is someone who owes

explanation.surface: A debtor acquires a rich property owner as a new man in their life.
explanation.definitionFit: A landowner holds real estate, so is literally a person possessing land and buildings.

clue.text: Chest covered by father's jacket

indicators.note: covered by says the first word is enclosed by the father's letters on both sides

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Something tucked under Dad's coat, such as a chest of his.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chest' looks like part of the body, which a jacket covers; here it is a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof coat, a kind of outdoor jacket.

clue.text: Bad accident with stain that won't dry

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A spill has left a mark that refuses to dry.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidesiccant prevents moisture loss, so something treated with it stays moist.

clue.text: Composer's right to abandon humorous work

definitions.note: Composer's here is 'composer is', linking the name to the wordplay

indicators.note: to abandon says the right's letter leaves the work

parts.note: a satire is a work that mocks through humour

explanation.surface: A composer is entitled to give up writing comic pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Composer's' is 'is': the composer is what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French musician who wrote the Gymnopédies, so he is a composer.

clue.text: Having gone without can?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside says the absent letters go round the can

parts.note: gone means absent, away
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Someone who has done without a can of beer is teetotal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as 'lacking' but is used in the old sense 'outside', and the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstinent person has refrained from drink, so has gone without a can of beer.

clue.text: Put in water and gently boiled after a delay of seconds

indicators.note: after a delay of says the seconds letter arrives later in the word than it started

parts.note: simmered means gently boiled

explanation.surface: Cooking instructions: an egg dropped in water and simmered after a pause of a few seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of SIMMERED moves from the front to near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Immersed means submerged, plunged below the surface of a liquid.

clue.text: Again appearing divided about good trick set up

indicators.note: about says the divided word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: rent means torn apart, divided

indicators.note: set up in a down clue reads the letters upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a ruse is a trick

explanation.surface: A divided group plotting a scheme again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns GRUSE into ESURG, which goes inside RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resurgent is rising again after a decline, reappearing in strength.

clue.text: Did cure set lad in order?

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Was it treatment that sorted the boy out?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cure' looks medical, but it means preserving meat or fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To salt meat is to cure it, preserving it with salt.

clue.text: Italian food free of charge on account, I note

parts.note: FOC is the abbreviation for free of charge
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: Getting Italian food for nothing by putting it on a tab.
explanation.definitionFit: Focaccia is a flat Italian bread topped with olive oil and herbs.

clue.text: Torturer is beginning to tremble after feeling sorrow

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the sorrowful word

parts.note: feeling sorrow means sad

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of the word tremble

explanation.surface: A torturer starts to shake after feeling remorse for what he did.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadist takes pleasure in inflicting pain, the hallmark of a torturer.

clue.text: Misrepresent sordid gossip about thug's head found in well

indicators.note: about says the gossip goes round the rest

parts.note: dirt is scandalous gossip

indicators.note: found in says the head letter sits inside the word well

parts.note: so is a filler word, like well

indicators.note: head takes the first letter of the thug

explanation.surface: Twisting scandal about a thug whose head was discovered down a well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like a water shaft; it is the interjection, SO.
explanation.definitionFit: To distort facts is to twist them, giving a false account.

clue.text: Note worn-out spirits or low spirits

parts.note: D is a musical note
worn-out means old
rums are spirits

explanation.surface: A choice between tired spirits and depression, the drinker's dilemma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' appears twice: first the drinks, then mood.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the doldrums is to be glum, in a state of gloom or depression.

clue.text: Armed criminal with no good lady, heartless like a female?

indicators.note: with no says the good letter is removed

parts.note: a gunman is an armed criminal

indicators.note: heartless removes the inside of the word lady, keeping its ends

explanation.surface: A gunman without a decent woman is callous, acting like a woman?
explanation.definitionFit: Unmanly means not befitting a man, which can suggest effeminacy; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: High priest takes pilgrimage up for prophet

parts.note: Eli was the high priest at Shiloh in the Bible

indicators.note: up in a down clue reads the pilgrimage word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the haj is the Muslim pilgrimage to Mecca

explanation.surface: A senior cleric goes on a pilgrimage in honour of a prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: Elijah was an Old Testament prophet taken to heaven in a fiery chariot.

clue.text: Uluru's place: rock as a ritual

indicators.note: to rock is to shake, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Uluru is a sacred rock where ceremonies are held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like Uluru itself, the great sandstone rock, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Uluru, also called Ayers Rock, is a landmark in the Northern Territory of that country.

clue.text: Copy three notes

definitions.meaning: to copy someone's voice or manner is to imitate them
read as MI, MI and C, three notes: mi twice from sol-fa, C from the letter-named scale

explanation.surface: A musical instruction to repeat three notes.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a string of notes spelt out in full: two sol-fa notes and a lettered one.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic is to imitate, reproducing another's words or manner.

clue.text: Yacht haven keeping out November seas

indicators.note: keeping out says the November letter is excluded

parts.note: a marina is a harbour for yachts
N is November in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A harbour shelters yachts from rough winter seas.
explanation.walkthrough: These are the dark plains on the Moon, not water.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria, plural of mare, are the lunar 'seas', dark basaltic plains on the Moon.

clue.text: Kindle returned some week overdue

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An e-reader (or library book) brought back a week late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kindle' suggests Amazon's e-reader and 'returned' a library loan; Kindle is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle a feeling or memory is to arouse it, which is to evoke it.

clue.text: What's about to be planted in pot with a tropical tree

indicators.note: to be planted in says the 'about' letters go inside the container

parts.note: a jar is a pot
CA, short for circa, is what means about
with means and

explanation.surface: Instructions for potting a tropical tree: put it in a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The jacaranda is a South American tree with blue-violet blossoms, grown in warm climates.

clue.text: Stupid person in school is a pain

indicators.note: in says the stupid person sits inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: tit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A dim pupil at school is a pain in the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sharp pain in the side, often brought on by running.

clue.text: Canal Street clubs won't open to admit unknown investigator

indicators.note: to admit says the shortened street letters let in the unknown
won't open says the clubs letter at the start goes

parts.note: taken as written
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Bars on Canal Street, Manchester's gay village, stay shut to a mysterious detective.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing C leaves ANALST; Y goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: An analyst examines things closely, so is a kind of investigator, as a financial or systems analyst is.
